note: Refresh cadence per list, and - the part that matters - what happens when a list is older than its budget. Every `onStale` value is a refusal of some kind. None of them is 'carry on with the old copy', because a screening stage running on a list nobody refreshed is a stage that reports CLEAR for the wrong reason. `cadence` is for the operator; `maxAgeSeconds` is the half the code enforces.

rules.cadence: daily 07:00 UTC, and again on any OFAC publication notice
rules.note: Matches DEFAULT_SDN_POLICY.maxListAgeSeconds in packages/screening/src/ofac.ts. This is the one list whose false negative has a legal consequence rather than a commercial one, so a stale list cannot produce a CLEAR at all - not merely 'no paid media'. The shipped cache is non-authoritative and empty, which fails the same way.

rules.cadence: weekly, Monday, with a monthly review of category coverage
rules.source: operator-controlled storage; digests computed with hashTerm() from @fee-split-vaults/catalog
rules.note: Slur lexicons churn: new coinages, new spellings, new numeric codes. A month-old list still catches the durable terms, which is why this blocks paid media rather than all screening - the coin can keep operating organically while the list is refreshed.

rules.cadence: monthly, and on any inbound trademark complaint
rules.source: data/screening/marks.json, maintained by the operator alongside counsel
rules.note: Marks and public figures move slowly, so the budget is a quarter. The complaint-driven half of the cadence is the one that actually matters: the list should grow every time someone writes to us.

rules.cadence: daily 06:00 UTC from the public feeds; on incident from our own chats
rules.note: 48 hours, because drainer infrastructure rotates hosts in hours. On staleness the desk stops posting links at all rather than posting them unchecked; the allowlist keeps the four links a project actually publishes working.

rules.cadence: daily, before the procurement window opens
rules.note: 26 hours, matching RATE_CARD_MAX_AGE_SECONDS. An unreconciled price is a price the operator could be marking up, so the SKU is disabled rather than sold with an asterisk.

rules.cadence: on change only; reviewed whenever a new fact field is added
rules.note: The schema is a declaration, not an observation, so it does not go stale on its own. The year budget exists so that a schema nobody has looked at in a year forces a review rather than quietly outliving the contracts it describes.
